newsitem.title: INDIA: India chemical sector could be world player - Ambani.
newsitem.headline: India chemical sector could be world player - Ambani.

text.p: India's chemical sector, which has only 1.3 percent of international trade, is a pygmy that has the potential of becoming a giant, a top official of India's largest private-sector petrochmicals firm said on Friday.

"We have a chemical industry in India that is marginal by global standards, highly fragmented, yet has an immense potential outlook," Mukesh Ambani, vice-chairman of Reliance Industries Ltd, told a meeting of Indian chemical manufacturers.
India's chemical industry has been a marginal player in the global arena, with $22 billion in value of output and a 1.5 percent share of the global chemical industry, Ambani said.
The country's per capita consumption of plastics and polyester fibres is also among the lowest in the world.
Reliance is India's leading polyester and plastics maker.
But Ambani said he believed all that would soon change.
"However, even by conservative estimates, the growth of the Indian chemical industry is placed at about 15 percent per annum," Ambani added. "Its output is expected to double in the next five years."
The projected growth rate worked out to almost twice that of the Asian growth rate and five times the world growth rate, he said.
"Therefore one is talking of the India chemical opportunity that is worth at least $400 billion over the next 15 years, twenty times bigger than today," Ambani said.

He urged the manufacturers to pull themselves out of their "cottage industry" mindset, and benchmark their strategies to global standards. Rather than spread themselves too thin, they must focus on niche areas to give them competitive strengths, Ambani said.
"We have to pool resources in reasearch and development set in an information technology framework and reduce cycle time from the laboratory to commercial production," Ambani stressed.
He wanted manufacturers to form partnerships with the federal government to open new markets and protect the industry from unfair competition, thus enabling it to become a global player.
